text: Around the beginning of the first century, Joseph lived in Nazareth in Galilee. He was a carpenter, working with his hands. He was promised in marriage to Mary. Then he learned that she was expecting a child. Matthew's Gospel calls Joseph a just man. He did not want to expose Mary to public shame, but he had a difficult decision before him.

text: In a dream, an angel told Joseph not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife. Her child was from the Holy Spirit. The angel told him to name the baby Jesus. When Joseph woke, he did what the angel had asked. He welcomed Mary as his wife. Caring for her and the child became part of the life he would share with them.

text: Joseph and Mary traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem. Luke's Gospel tells us that Jesus was born there. Mary wrapped him and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place. A manger was a feeding trough, not a grand cradle. In this simple place, Mary and Joseph cared for the child Christians call God's Son.

text: Joseph gave the baby the name Jesus, as the angel had told him. He was not Jesus' biological father, but he accepted the responsibility of being his earthly father and guardian. The family's life had begun with a journey and a birth far from Nazareth. Now another journey would ask Joseph to act quickly to keep the child safe.

text: An angel warned Joseph in a dream that Herod wanted to harm Jesus. Joseph rose, took Mary and the child during the night, and left for Egypt. They stayed there while Herod was alive. Leaving meant becoming a family far from home, but it took the child away from danger. Joseph's care for Jesus now meant finding safety in another land.

text: After Herod died, an angel again appeared to Joseph in a dream. Joseph brought Mary and Jesus back. But he learned that Herod's son was ruling in Judea, and he was afraid to go there. Warned in another dream, he went to Galilee. The family settled in Nazareth. The journeys had brought them to the town where Jesus would grow up.

text: When Jesus was twelve, they took him to Jerusalem for Passover. On the way home, Mary and Joseph realized he was not with their traveling group. They searched among relatives and friends, then returned to Jerusalem. After three days, they found him in the Temple. He was listening to the teachers and asking questions. Mary told him how worried they had been. If you are separated from your caregivers, ask a safe, trusted adult for help.

text: Jesus returned with Mary and Joseph to Nazareth and was obedient to them. He grew in wisdom and age. Joseph's care had carried the family through a birth, danger, journeys, and a search for their missing child. At home again, their daily life continued. Christians remember Joseph for this faithful care. The carpenter of Nazareth had made a home for Jesus and stayed beside him as he grew.

title: Points of reflection
points: First, Joseph chose not to shame Mary. When someone is confused or afraid, how can you treat them with kindness while asking a trusted adult for help if needed?
Second, Joseph moved his family away from danger. Courage is not staying where you are unsafe. Which trusted adult can you tell if you or someone else needs protection?

Third, his carpentry and daily care mattered. What small, useful thing could you do at home without expecting praise? Rest and play matter too; you are a child, not the one responsible for your family's safety.
Fourth, Mary and Joseph asked and searched when Jesus was missing. If you get separated from your caregivers, which safe helper could help you find them? Asking for help is wise, not weak.
text:
Joseph's care sometimes meant leaving home and sometimes returning to ordinary work. Which moment in his story shows you something about caring for a family? Talk about it together.

Read Luke, chapter two, verses fifty-one and fifty-two with someone who cares for you. Jesus returns to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph, and grows in wisdom and age. This passage brings us back to their life at home.

Try one useful kindness at home today. You could put something away or help with a task that fits your age.

God, thank you for the people who care for me. Help me notice when someone needs kindness, and give me the courage to ask for help. Saint Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
